exposure: oxytocin bolus protocol followed by infusion
cohort: The study included patients who underwent cesarean deliveries at a single Texas hospital during specified periods in 2021 and 2022.
finding: Patients receiving oxytocin boluses followed by an infusion during cesarean delivery were approximately 75% less likely to receive a secondary uterotonic agent compared to those who received an oxytocin infusion without boluses.
mod_finding: The implementation of an oxytocin bolus protocol during cesarean delivery significantly reduced the need for secondary uterotonic agents compared to an oxytocin infusion-only protocol.
